messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty Alert fired for service=redwood-serving-prod, alert=GPU memory pressure (cuda allocation failures) on node redwood-gpu-12. severity=high. link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 created and triggered. Escalation policy: eng-oncall. Initial urgency: high.

sam (oncall): acked the incident. I'm looking. Seeing repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` in the pod logs.

sam (oncall): logs excerpt:
```
I0306 14:22:10.123 Serving] model=llama2-13b worker=wg-7: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
E0306 14:22:10.124 KVCache] failed to allocate 512MB for cache: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
E0306 14:22:10.125 Runtime] Fatal: nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo returned error -3
```

sam (oncall): metric spike: GPU memory usage 98%, OOM kills on 3 pods in the pool. Throughput dropped, some requests 500.

maya (oncall-lead): pinging infra to check node-level NVidia driver/firmware. Maya: any recent deploys to that pool?

priya: no deploys to that pool in the last hour. We had an autoscaler bounce last night. I'll check node drift and kube events.

infra-bot: node redwood-gpu-12 reports `OutOfMemory` from nvidia-smi query. Container runtimes show multiple `OOM` events. GPU driver version 525.60.13.

support-eng: FYI support: customers CUST-489, CUST-501, and CUST-502 reporting high error rates for text-generation endpoints. We routed them to fallback model but some telemetry shows degraded quality for fallback.

sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) cordon redwood-gpu-12 2) drain non-critical pods 3) scale up alternate GPU pool redwood-gpu-2 (if capacity) 4) temporarily reduce per-request kv cache and batch size via config override 5) fallback route heavy requests to cpu-small model. Applying step 1 now.

sam (oncall): `kubectl cordon redwood-gpu-12` -> success. Starting `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data redwood-gpu-12`

priya: I'm spinning up 2 nodes in redwood-gpu-2 and bumping capacity by +2 (requested from autoscaler). ETA ~3m.

sam (oncall): config patch to reduce kv cache size and max_batch_size applied to modelserving configmap (canary route):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  kv_cache_size: "256MB"
  max_batch_size: "4"
```

nora: routing rule updated: heavy routes fallback to `llama2-7b-quant` for 10% of traffic using canary policy.

pagerduty-bot: Sam acknowledged at 2026-03-06T14:23:11Z. Incident assigned to sam.

maya (oncall-lead): escalation check: if nodes don't stabilize in 10m escalate to infra-sre@redwood and runbook step 3 (nvml driver restart).

sam (oncall): after drain, two pods evicted; relaunching on redwood-gpu-2. Observed one pod failing to start with same OOM right after scheduling. Suspect model config or corrupted cache state persisted.

priya: checking PVCs and temp storage mounts. If cache persisted on host, might be rehydrating and causing OOM. I'll bind mount to empty dir for new pods.

support-eng: customer-impact summary: 3 customers with elevated 5xx and slow responses. Impact window started 14:21Z. Estimated affected requests ~1.2k over 10m. Not yet P0 customer outage but degrading SLAs.

sam (oncall): temporary hotfix: set `PERSIST_KV=false` for the canary group and restart pods. Doing rolling restart of canary subset.

infra-bot: action: restarted 4 pods with PERSIST_KV=false. New pods report GPU memory use ~62% steady, no immediate OOM.

sam (oncall): metrics look better: error rate dropping, latency returning to baseline. Keeping incident open to monitor 30m.

maya (oncall-lead): good. Sam, please prepare a short handoff for the next oncall. Include what we changed, affected customers, and followups.

sam (oncall): Handoff for next oncall (Priya at 18:00Z):
- Root symptom: repeated cuda memory allocation failures on redwood-gpu-12 causing OOMs.
- Actions taken: cordon/drain node, reduced kv cache and batch size, disabled persistent KV for canary pods, scaled up alternate GPU pool, routed heavy traffic to smaller model canary.
- Customer impact: 3 customers degraded; requests affected ~1.2k between 14:21-14:31Z; fallbacks in place, quality slightly degraded for fallback.
- Next steps / followups: run full nvml driver diag on redwood-gpu-12, verify driver version and any recent firmware updates, investigate why persisted KV caused rehydration OOM (ticket INFRA-789), consider adding eviction tolerations and preemptive pod placement rules.
- Runbook refs: runbook/gpu-memory-pressure.md step 2-4.

priya: acked handoff. I'll monitor 30m and follow up on INFRA-789. If there's any regression I'll escalate.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 status: acknowledged -> in_progress. Pls update timeline as you make changes.

incident-bot: Note added to incident: `PERSIST_KV disabled for canary; node cordoned; scaled up redwood-gpu-2; customer impact mitigated; monitoring 30m.`

nora: leaving a short post for postmortem: suspected persisted cache rehydrate + high batch sizes pushed memory beyond host capacity; will collect heap dumps and nvml logs.

sam (oncall): closing update: at 14:28Z error rates back to baseline for all routes, CPU/GPU metrics stable. Keeping channel open for 30m, will escalate if we see new OOMs. :white_check_mark:
